subject: Commercial options for HyperServe: credits vs prepay
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@hyperserve.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial options for HyperServe: credits vs prepay

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together two pragmatic commercial paths so your procurement and finance teams can evaluate impact quickly. High level: we can either do a prepay (upfront commitment with a material discount) or a credits-based onramp that cushions the first months while you validate runtime economics.

Attached: HS-commercial-alignment-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet walks through net spend under both options)

Quick summary:
- Option A — 12-month prepay: 18% ARR-equivalent discount, includes 2 weeks priority onboarding and 1 dedicated onboarding session (up to 40 hours).
- Option B — Credits + usage: $150k in one-time credits applied to first three billing cycles + a $25k onboarding credit; standard pay-as-you-go rates thereafter. Credits amortize over 12 months for internal reporting.

Questions I need from you to finalize numbers for procurement:
1) Do you prefer credits amortized over 12 or 24 months for internal chargeback?
2) Any constraints around covering egress or third-party infra costs with credits (we typically exclude egress).
3) Target legal/billing contact so we can prep a short SOW and signature flow.

If useful I can block 30 min tomorrow to walk the worksheet with your finance lead.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
[k] +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Karthik — the worksheet is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from our side before we pull procurement into a deeper review:

1) Amortization: our finance team prefers a 24-month amortization for one-off credits to smooth P&L — any flexibility?
2) Egress & infra pass-through: will the credits cover egress charges if we route traffic across a partner region?
3) Can you share a sample SOW and an example billing schedule that shows the timing of credits hitting ledger?

Looping in procurement so they have visibility — I tagged our procurement alias. I attached our RFP extract where we called out egress and data-retention expectations.

Appreciate it,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Platform Partnerships
HyperServe

Olivia / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick notes. Short answers and a proposed clean commercial structure so your procurement and finance teams can compare side-by-side:

Amortization flexibility: we can support a 24-month amortization on the credits for your internal reporting (we'll reflect that on an internal invoice schedule; accounting memo available on request).
Egress: credits do not cover third-party cloud egress or marketplace fees. If you need a pass-through carve-out, we can include a capped egress credit line in Option A as an exception.

Two concrete proposals (numbers illustrative until we receive precise usage profiles):

- Option 1 — Prepay (12 mo): $1,200,000 prepay for committed usage (covers inference + base observability) with 18% discount off list. Includes 40 hours of onboarding and 2 priority support incidents during first 90 days. We can add a $30k capped egress credit as an add-on.

- Option 2 — Credits + PAYG: $150k one-time credits + $25k onboarding credit applied against first three invoices. Credits are amortized over 24 months in your ledger per your preference. After credits, standard pay-as-you-go rates. We also include a 6-week technical enablement package.

Next steps I propose:
- I will upload a short SOW draft and a commercial worksheet that maps the two options to your typical monthly burn.
- If procurement agrees, we can bake the preferred amortization language into the commercial attachment and route to legal via DocuSign.

Shared links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid/hyperserve-commercial-alignment (SOW + worksheet)

Attached: SOW-draft-Redwood-HyperServe.pdf

Open to a 30-min call tomorrow; Avery and Grace are on copy to help with technical and billing questions.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
